writes move off the twg CLI onto hall9k\\u0027s own REST client: the compose-execute split, validation, event-stream recording, and retry machinery stay exactly as they are while the executor\\u0027s transport becomes the same authenticated Jira Cloud v2 API the read provider already uses - so a write\\u0027s outcome is a structured JSON response instead of a parsed text envelope, the process-spawning fragility and version-drift risk retire with the twg dependency, and one registered connection credential covers both directions\\u0022\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022\\u0022The run\\u0027s opening act is re-examining Decisions Log #102 (twg as the sole write executor): the PR description records whether the original rationale still binds, and if a genuinely binding reason surfaces - a capability twg provides that the Jira Cloud v2 REST API lacks - the run parks with that finding instead of proceeding\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022Card creates (work item type, built-in and custom fields) and comment writes execute through hall9k\\u0027s own REST client against the Jira Cloud v2 API, authenticated by the registered connection (email plus API token), with no process spawn on the write path\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022The compose-execute split is unchanged in behavior: agents compose payloads, h9k task write-jira remains the sole executor, and payload validation, intent and outcome events on the task stream, the retry engine, pending-write ceilings, and merge-notice drains all behave identically - the swap is the transport layer only, and the coordinator\\u0027s integration tests pass without behavioral edits\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022The verified read-back and dedup guarantees survive with structured semantics: read-back fetches the card via REST and verifies content from JSON fields, the dedup marker search parses the card\\u0027s actual description field rather than any raw output text, and the create-ambiguity class (a write sent but no confirmed key) is handled by HTTP status semantics, retaining the check-the-board-before-retrying guidance for the one genuinely ambiguous case of a timeout after the request was sent\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022The cancellation-grace behavior around post-write bookkeeping saves is preserved as-is - a daemon stop landing between a successful write and its recording still cannot strand a posted comment as pending\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022twg is no longer required for any h9k or h9kd operation: the login prerequisite, TwgDoctor\\u0027s checks, and install or help surfaces that name twg are retired or narrowed to nothing, and the docs say the registered connection\\u0027s API token now covers writes\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022Executor tests fake HTTP responses instead of process output envelopes, covering the status-code classes the old envelope parsing guarded (success with key, 4xx refusal, auth failure, timeout-after-send), and the full suite passes in the foreground before the run concludes\\u0022\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Refactor\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nDrafted 2026-08-31 from the b6dfcbe5 retrospective: the Jira compose-execute task cost 55 review cycles across nine generations, and the dominant defect class was twg\\u0027s opacity - regex-parsing its output envelope for temp-file paths, blank stdout ambiguity, create-exited-clean-but-no-key, exit-code conventions verified empirically per version, and a dedup gate reduced to substring-searching envelope text (the cycle-10/11 medium). Every one of those exists because the write channel\\u0027s answers are text a human meant to read. The read side (JiraWorkItemProvider) already talks to the same API with the same registered credential and has none of this class.\\n\\nWhat this deliberately keeps: the compose-execute split and everything above the transport (Brian\\u0027s ruling, Decisions Log #102\\u0027s split itself is not in question - only the executor\\u0027s vehicle). The hard-won write-safety logic (verified read-back, dedup markers, cancellation graces, retry budgets) is still required; it just gets structured responses to stand on.\\n\\nSecondary win, and the thread that surfaced this: one credential per install. The Windows machine\\u0027s install asked for an API token on top of twg login; after this, the token alone covers both directions and the twg binary need not exist on a node.\\n\\nPriority ruling (Brian, 2026-08-31): queue at the back, no jump - \\u0022as we chew through work, it\\u0027ll get done at some point.\\u0022 The #102 re-examination gate makes it safe to queue without a prior walk of migration. \\u0060TaskDecider.ClaimInteractively\\u0060 requires Queued, the same state the dispatcher feeds on, and \\u0060h9k task assign\\u0060 itself sends the Postgres NOTIFY that rings \\u0060DispatchLoop\\u0060\\u0027s doorbell - so on an idle node with a free slot the daemon essentially always wins the window between an operator\\u0027s \\u0060assign\\u0060 and their \\u0060work\\u0060. The race never bit on the original dev machine only because its ceiling of 1 keeps a run in flight and Queued tasks lingering. If the daemon wins, there is no kill lever (the pause-state idea was evaluated and rejected for blast radius, 2026-08-30), so the operator waits out a headless run they never wanted.\\n\\nThe interim workaround, documented so the fix can retire it: stop the daemon around the claim (\\u0060h9k daemon stop\\u0060, \\u0060publish --assign\\u0060, \\u0060task work\\u0060, \\u0060daemon start\\u0060).\\n\\nDesign ruling (Brian, 2026-08-31): \\u0060assign --interactive\\u0060 was proposed and rejected in favor of this shape. The deciding property: an interactive claim already expresses \\u0022reserve now, work later\\u0022 - it has no lease and no heartbeat, closing the terminal is a normal way to leave, and re-entry is designed-normal - so a single atomic \\u0060task work\\u0060 covers both \\u0022mine, now\\u0022 and \\u0022mine, later\\u0022 with all existing machinery (stale-claim nudge, release, handback) attached, the same reasoning that let \\u0060publish --assign\\u0060 collapse a step.\\n\\n## Sequencing\\n\\nPriority ruling (Brian, 2026-08-31): queue behind the current chain - the daemon-stop workaround fully covers the near-term need.
